key_insight: Silicon oxynitride-doped silicon enables laser-inscribed flexible Bragg gratings fabricated below 100 °C for multispectral authentication.
engineering_relevance: Low-temperature processing, photosensitivity, and refractive-index control from 2.1 to 2.5 offer a route to flexible photonic security features.
method: Synthesize silicon oxynitride-doped silicon films on flexible substrates and inscribe Bragg gratings with ultrafast lasers.
Probe local structure using soft X-ray absorption at the Si L, O K, and N K edges.
Investigate formation mechanisms with quantum calculations and predict bulk Si3N4−xOx structures using particle swarm optimization with DFT.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical and experimental demonstrations of micro-information preservation through multispectral reflection from UV to near-infrared wavelengths.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify authentication performance or durability under repeated bending and environmental exposure.
paper_title: Design and synthesis of laser inscribed flexible Bragg gratings containing silicon oxynitride-doped silicon thin film for authentication applications with the insights from X-Ray Absorption Spectroscopy and Quantum Mechanical Calculations
